We are not responsible for any problems resulting from creating a custom resolution on your PC.

It may be that your monitor does not support a necessary display configuration. If so, you may try to set up a virtual monitor. Finally, if your device or host PC does not support streaming at a specific resolution or refresh rate, you're out of luck unfortunately.

Vulkan adds dithering and native frame pacing. Automatic uses the direct renderer.

Not yet tried with a real Turnip driver. Loads a Vulkan driver file you choose, such as Turnip, for PyroWave on 64-bit ARM devices with Android 10 or newer; other codecs keep the system driver. If the driver can\'t load or can\'t run PyroWave, the system driver is used instead, but a driver that crashes closes Starwire. Restart Starwire after changing it.
Tap to choose the driver (.so, .zip or .adpkg). Starwire checks it\'s a 64-bit ARM library, then copies it into its own storage.
%1$s was imported by an older Starwire that didn\'t record its SHA-256, so it isn\'t used. Tap to choose it again.
Could not import the custom driver
Deletes the driver file from Starwire\'s storage.

This loads a graphics driver file that you choose into Starwire. It's only used for PyroWave streams.

The driver runs as part of Starwire, with the same access as the app: your network, your microphone if you've allowed it, and the keys for your paired PCs. Only use a driver file from a source you trust.

If the driver can't load or can't run PyroWave, Starwire goes back to the normal driver. A driver that crashes closes Starwire instead.

Keeps the Wi-Fi connection busy with a tiny packet every 20 ms, so devices that drop packets in Wi-Fi power saving stay awake. Uses slightly more battery.
Where the host streams from. Host default leaves it to Vibepollo\'s own setting.

Direct renderer only. V-Sync holds each frame for the next screen refresh (adds up to one frame of latency). Fast V-Sync spaces frames evenly when the stream FPS matches the screen (Prefer lowest latency pacing only). Ignored with the Vulkan renderer and host frame timing pacing.
Balanced pacing on the direct renderer: discard frames that are already stale when decoded and show only the newest. May drop more frames under load. The other pacing modes already do this.
The decoder reports ready frames as they happen instead of being checked in a loop. Direct renderer only, not with host frame timing. Turn off if video stalls or stutters.
With async decode, keep only the newest decoded frame waiting to be shown, for the lowest delay. May drop more frames under load.
Vibrate when keys on the on-screen full keyboard are pressed
On the on-screen full keyboard, long-press Ctrl, Alt, Shift or Win to hold it down; tap it again to let go
How see-through the on-screen full keyboard is

Send this device\'s clipboard to the PC when the stream starts or you return to it, and copy the PC\'s clipboard here when you leave the stream. Needs clipboard permission for this device in Vibepollo.
Show a short message each time the clipboard is synced automatically
Mark text copied from the PC as sensitive, so Android doesn\'t preview it on screen
Warp Drive: 2x FPS from the PC, newest frame shown (Experimental)
Warp 2: 4x FPS from the PC, newest frame shown (Experimental)

Hide the PC\'s mouse cursor in the video, using Vibepollo\'s Ctrl+Alt+Shift+N toggle. It\'s shown again when the stream ends, or the next time you connect if Starwire was closed suddenly. If it\'s ever the wrong way round, use Fix PC Cursor in the stream menu.
Switched the PC cursor. If it\'s still wrong, tap Fix PC Cursor again.
The PC cursor was left hidden last time, so Starwire turned it back on.
Each frame is shown as soon as it arrives. Inputs feel quick, but motion can stutter on a busy network.
Frames are lined up with the screen and late ones are skipped. A good default for most games.
Like Balanced, with the PC sending no more frames than this screen shows.
Every frame is shown in order, so motion is the smoothest, but the delay can grow a lot.
Frames are shown on the PC\'s own timing. Steady motion, best with the Vulkan renderer.
The PC sends twice the frames and the newest one is always shown. Lower delay, but the tablet, PC and network work harder.
The PC sends four times the frames and the newest one is always shown. The lowest delay, with the most work for the tablet, PC and network.
V-Sync stops tearing but can add up to one frame of delay.
Fast V-Sync spaces frames evenly when the stream matches the screen.
Async LFR keeps only the newest decoded frame waiting.

Run Starwire\'s microphone setup on the PC once. It installs VB-Cable (a free virtual microphone) and Starwire\'s receiver. Then pair with the PC below, and choose CABLE Output as the microphone in Discord or the game. Tap for the guide.

Not encrypted: anyone on the same network can listen to your microphone or send sound into the PC\'s microphone. Use it only for Voicemeeter or another VBAN app, on a network you trust. Set it to receive stream %2$s from %1$s (or this device\'s VPN address over a VPN), port %3$d, and play it into CABLE Input; then choose CABLE Output as the microphone in Discord or the game. Higher is sharper but needs more bandwidth and decode time. Lower helps slower devices and networks.
Higher is smoother and lowers latency, but uses more battery and bandwidth.
Higher gives a cleaner picture but needs a faster connection. Too high for your Wi-Fi causes stutter.
Lowest latency can tear or stutter. The smoother options add a little latency.
A bigger buffer rides out patchy Wi-Fi but adds latency.
On removes tearing but adds up to one frame of latency.
On lowers latency by skipping late frames. Motion can look less even under load.
On can cut decode delay on some devices (not measured in Starwire yet). Turn it off if video stalls.
On gives the lowest delay but can drop frames under load.
Can lower decode latency on the chips listed. No gain on others; turn it off if video glitches.
Surround uses a little more bandwidth. No change to latency.
Can add audio delay. Leave it off unless you use an equalizer.
Uses a little upload bandwidth and battery. No change to video.

Over the stream it\'s compressed to about 24 kbps. To a receiver on the PC it goes uncompressed, just under 1 Mbps, and only to a PC on your home network or a private VPN. Starwire\'s receiver gets it encrypted; the other VBAN option isn\'t encrypted. No change to video.
Uses some battery. No change to the stream.
Lower feels more responsive, but worn sticks may drift.
For devices whose Wi-Fi naps between packets. Slightly more battery.
90 or 120 FPS can lower latency on fast devices but can lag on slower ones.
Saves battery but adds some latency.
A wrong value makes pacing stutter. 0 measures it for you.
HEVC and AV1 look better at the same bitrate. Older devices can take longer to decode them.
Accepting more blur keeps the stream smooth when frames arrive late.
Vulkan paces frames more evenly for a small GPU cost. Direct has the least overhead.
Experimental and not yet tried with a real Turnip driver. A bad driver can close Starwire.
Small GPU cost. No change to latency.
Uses 10-bit video, which needs hardware HEVC or AV1 decoding. Slower devices may take longer per frame.
Very small. Lite mode draws less.
